texts: How a three.ws model is rendered, from a sentence to a lit, rigged character in your browser tab

A glTF file, Three.js and WebGL on the viewer's own GPU: no plugin, no video, no server drawing frames. That is how three.ws renders 3D, and the Article follows one rigged character through making, packing, loading, lighting and animating, with the embed code, the free checking tools, our partners and the roadmap.

issues.quote: The AWS Marketplace listing is built and waiting on product creation, the NVIDIA catalog submissions are in review, an OpenAI Cookbook contribution is submitted, and a Microsoft Azure Marketplace listing is on the roadmap.
issues.problem: These are promises about the future and marketplace states with no evidence and no verification result. A promise about a listing, submission or review with no evidence is a blocking issue.
issues.fix: Delete the entire "What is next" section, or cut it to the one item that could be evidenced by a file in the repository (none is supplied). The article ends cleanly on the partners section followed by "Try it".

issues.quote: three.ws is listed on the Alibaba Cloud International Marketplace, and Qwen models are lanes in the platform's model router.
issues.problem: No claim in the verification set covers the Alibaba Cloud listing or Qwen router lanes, so these factual statements are unverified.
issues.fix: Remove the Alibaba Cloud paragraph, or supply a passing verification (a partner JSON file or live page check) and restore the exact designation it states.

issues.quote: three.ws is accepted into the Quicknode Startup Program, and Quicknode's RPC endpoints are a rung in the Solana failover chain.
issues.problem: No verification result covers Quicknode. Unverified partnership claim.
issues.fix: Remove the Quicknode paragraph, or supply a passing partner-file check and state the designation exactly as the file states it.

issues.quote: three.ws has partnered with HackerNoon, whose import picks up our announcements for its developer audience.
issues.problem: No verification result covers HackerNoon. Unverified partnership claim.
issues.fix: Remove the HackerNoon paragraph, or supply a passing partner-file check.

issues.quote: How a three.ws model is rendered, from a sentence to a lit, rigged character in your browser tab
issues.problem: The Article standard requires the title to carry the headline number; this title carries none, despite the article having strong verified numbers (52 bones, 53 tracks, 90 percent size saving).
issues.fix: Retitle to: "How three.ws renders 3D: one sentence to a 52-bone rigged character, drawn live in your browser tab" (92 characters, both numbers verified).

issues.quote: the canonicaliser to more skeleton conventions
issues.problem: The codebase names the module glb-canonicalize (American spelling) while the article mixes "canonicaliser" with "canonicalize.js". Flagged by the spelling check. Pick one spelling; the file's own spelling is the safer choice for a developer audience.
issues.fix: Change "canonicaliser" to "canonicalizer" so it matches the module name `src/glb-canonicalize.js`.

editor.summary: The article is deep, well-shaped and almost entirely verified, but the "What is next" section makes unsupported forward-looking claims and three partner paragraphs (Alibaba Cloud, Quicknode, HackerNoon) have no verification at all; all four must be cut or evidenced before this ships. The promo post and visuals are fine as they are, and the title needs a verified headline number to meet the Article standard.
